rationale: The ground-truth concerns center on two threads: rigor/completeness of the target-hardware validation numbers, and whether Ref2VA had actually been tested (it had a bug, later fixed). Candidate X's findings (README indexing, RTX PRO 5000 phrasing, numactl flags, curl audio syntax, peak-memory header mismatch) are well-evidenced but orthogonal to both threads, giving it almost no recall. Candidate Y directly engages both: it flags that Ref2VA was 'never measured' and warns of foreseeable OOM/restart failures on that path (echoing the reviewer's 'have you tested ref2va mode?'), and separately attacks the validation section's rigor (undersampled 1Hz peak-memory claim, unsupported 0.25% precision) mirroring the human's demand for methodological completeness. Y also independently reproduces X's numactl-flag catch and adds a solid, verifiable GDDR7-vs-HBM mislabeling finding, suggesting reasonable grounding despite its much larger volume of claims. Both are concrete and file/line-anchored, but Y's added depth and thematic overlap with the actual review thread give it a clear recall advantage that outweighs its slightly higher fabrication risk from sheer claim volume.
